newsitem.title: USA: Major stock market movements overnight - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: Major stock market movements overnight - Aug 1.

text.p: NEW YORK - U.S. blue chips moved in a range near Wednesday's closing levels in late trade. Traders said action appeared subdued ahead of Friday's report on July employment, although a firm bond market provided support. By 7.45 a.m. NZT the Dow was down 23.45 points at 8,231.36.

LONDON - UK shares ended lower for the first time this week, unsettled by declines on Wall Street and renewed talk of an imminent UK interest rate rise. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,907.5, down 19.8 points, or 0.40 percent.

FRANKFURT - The share market ended more than one percent lower, despite earlier notching up fresh record gains, as the Dow Jones index on Wall Street moved lower and market players took profits. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,438.93, up 17.21 points, or 0.39 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,405.52, down 53.14 points, or 1.19 percent.

PARIS - Shares firmed to a fresh record close but came off the day's high after being dented by the U.S. Chicago Purchasing Managers Index that stoked inflationary fears, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 3,075.67, up 6.37 points, or 0.21 percent.
ZURICH - Shares ended lower as investors took profits ahead of a three-day weekend in Switzerland. The Swiss market index closed at 5,898.2, down 31.3 points, or 0.53 percent.

MILAN - Stocks tumbled by the close as selling set in first on futures and then in cash after Wall Street and bonds slid following a rise in part of the July Chicago Purchasing Managers Index. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14,694, down 111 points, or 0.75 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares held most of their early gains to close higher after stronger-than-expected earnings from chemicals group Akzo Nobel and the central bank left key interest rates unchanged. The AEX index closed at 983.33, up 8.02 points, or 0.82 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks ended higher as buying of blue chips accelerated in late afternoon, erasing losses created by racketeer scandal worries and a limping construction sector, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,331.43, up 118.61 points, or 0.59 percent.

HONG KONG - The Hang Seng Index closed at an all-time high, as investors poured into the property sector boosting turnover to its highest level ever. The Hang Seng index closed at 16,365.71, up 382.53 points, or 2.39 percent.

SYDNEY - A lacklustre share market limped to a flat finish with a bullish streak on Wall Street ignored in favour of a wary eye on the upcoming local profit season. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,735.1, up 0.1 points, or 0.00 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial shares finished stronger, propelled higher by positive sentiment from Wall Street and other world market's recent rallies, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,484.5, up 10.8 points, or 0.14 percent. The All Gold index closed at 981.4, down 1.2 points, or 0.31 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9,150.5, up 28.1 points, or 0.12 percent.
